newsitem.title: USA: CMS says 4 towers still down after storm.
newsitem.headline: CMS says 4 towers still down after storm.

text.p: CMS Energy Corp said Thursday that four of six towers supporting a main 345 kilovolt (kv) power transmission line were still down following violent thunderstorms in southeastern Michigan late Wednesday.

"We lost six large towers. They were on the ground...Two of them are repaired and we expect the rest of them to be up again sometime today," said Jon Hall, a spokesman for the Dearborn, Mich.-based power company.
The 345 kv line runs south from CMS's Karn-Weadock power generating complex in Essexville, Mich., to a major interconnect with the neighboring Detroit Edison power grid, he said.
Hall said the storm had also knocked out the company's 237 megawatt gas turbine power plant in Thetford, Mich., about 70 miles north of Detroit.

"The Thetford station was impacted rather severely. But its a peaking power station, not a baseload station," he said. He did not give an estimate for how long it would take to repair the power plant.
Despite damage to CMS's system, only about 4,000 of its customers were still without powwer early Thursday, compared with about 40,000 late Wednesday, Hall said.
He said the utility did not anticipate problems meeting electricity demand, saying their power supply was stable and loads were expected to be significantly less than Wednesday.
"It's about 20 degrees (Fahrenheit) cooler here today than it was yesterday," he said.
